blocks.text: Cost every job before you quote

Many new cleaners quote a figure that sounds fair and later find they made nothing. Always cost four things: **supplies** used on the job, **transport** there and back, **labour** for every person and every hour, including yourself, and **equipment wear**, a small amount set aside to replace mops, brushes and buckets. Add these for the **total cost**, then add your **profit**.

blocks.title: Worked example: pricing a deep clean of a three-bedroom flat
blocks.context: For example, Blessing in Abuja is asked to deep clean a three-bedroom flat before a family moves in. She visits first and estimates 5 hours of work for herself and one helper. All prices are approximate.
steps: Supplies (detergent, bleach, toilet cleaner, sponges, bin bags): about 2,000 naira.
Transport for both of them there and back: about 1,500 naira.
Labour: 2 people x 5 hours x 800 naira an hour = 8,000 naira.
Equipment wear: 500 naira set aside per job.
Profit of 25% on cost: 12,000 x 0.25 = 3,000 naira. Price: 12,000 + 3,000 = 15,000 naira.
blocks.result: Blessing quotes 15,000 naira (approximate) in writing. If she does 8 jobs like this a month, sales are 8 x 15,000 = 120,000 naira and profit after paying all costs, including her own labour, is 8 x 3,000 = 24,000 naira.

blocks.text: Notice that Blessing pays herself for her hours as part of labour, and the profit is extra money for the business to grow, buy better equipment or cover a slow month. If a job takes longer than estimated, note why and adjust your next quote rather than quietly losing money.
Check your price against the market

Your cost-based price is the minimum you can accept without losing money. Before you quote, ask two or three cleaners or customers in your area what similar jobs usually cost. If your price is far above theirs, look for savings: buy supplies in bulk, group jobs in the same area to cut transport, or offer a smaller package such as kitchen and bathroom only. If your price is well below the market, you may be undervaluing your time; raise it gradually as your references grow. Never cut costs by skipping gloves, diluting products below the label strength or rushing toilet cleaning, because those shortcuts are exactly what customers notice and stop paying for.

For hygiene sessions with women's groups or schools, cost your time to prepare, your transport, any handouts you print and the soap and water you use for the demonstration, then agree a fee or a sponsor in advance. Teach only what this course and WHO guidance support, and refer health questions about illness and medicines to a health worker.
Work safely and honestly

items: Give a written quote that lists what is included (rooms, toilet, kitchen, windows) and what is not.
Use a printed checklist for each job and walk through it with the customer at the end.
Bring your own gloves and keep toilet tools separate; follow every chemical label and never mix products.
Do not offer fumigation or pest poisoning unless you are trained and the products are registered for that use.
Do not claim that your cleaning 'kills all germs' or prevents a named disease. Say what you actually do: clean, disinfect high-risk surfaces and leave the home tidy.
Agree payment terms before you start, for example a deposit with the balance by bank transfer or a payment app on completion, and give a receipt.

blocks.title: Get your first references
blocks.text: Do two or three jobs for neighbours at a fair price, take before and after photos with their permission, and ask them for a short WhatsApp message you can show new customers. Real, permitted reviews build trust faster than adverts.
Keep a simple record for each job: date, customer, hours, costs, price and payment received. After a month you will know your real cost per job and which services earn the most.

takeaways: Pick a hygiene service that matches your skills and local demand.
Cost supplies, transport, labour for every person including you, and equipment wear.
Price = total cost + profit; check it with a monthly projection.
Use written quotes, job checklists and a customer walk-through.
Make no health claims you cannot support and never offer pesticide work without training.

activity.title: Cost and quote your first job
steps: Choose one service from the table that suits you.
Write a job checklist for it based on what you learned in this course.
Cost one realistic job: supplies, transport, labour, equipment wear.
Add a profit percentage and write a one-page quote.
Calculate sales and profit for 4 and 8 such jobs a month.
activity.evidence: Your job checklist, costing sheet and written quote

quiz.q: Joy's son spills boiling water on his arm. What should she do first?
options: Burst the blisters to release the heat
Cool the burn under cool, clean running water
quiz.explain: Cooling with clean running water is the correct first step. Oil, toothpaste and bursting blisters can worsen the injury or cause infection.

quiz.q: A child drinks kerosene that was stored in a soft drink bottle. What is the right response?
options: Go to the nearest health facility immediately and take the container
Give palm oil to neutralise it
Wait to see if symptoms appear
quiz.explain: Do not induce vomiting. Take the child straight to care with the container so the health worker knows what was swallowed.

quiz.q: A baby has passed 3 loose stools since morning. According to WHO, this is:
options: Diarrhoea, so start ORS and keep breastfeeding while watching for danger signs
Only diarrhoea if there is blood
quiz.explain: WHO defines diarrhoea as 3 or more loose or liquid stools a day. Start ORS, keep feeding and breastfeeding, and check danger signs.

quiz.q: Which sign means a child with diarrhoea should go to a health facility now?
options: The child is playing between stools
The child is passing normal amounts of urine
quiz.explain: WHO advises seeing a health worker when there is blood in the stool. The other signs are reassuring.

quiz.q: A job needs supplies 1,800 naira, transport 1,200 naira, labour 6,000 naira and equipment wear 500 naira. With 20% profit on cost, what is the price?
A customer asks Zainab to fumigate her house against rats. Zainab has no pest-control training. What should she do?
options: Buy any rat poison and do it
Decline the poisoning work, offer the cleaning and pest-proofing she is trained for, and refer the rest
Promise the home will be rat-free forever
Mix several insecticides for a stronger effect
quiz.explain: Pesticide work needs training and registered products. She can honestly offer cleaning, safe food storage and sealing holes, which she has learned.

finalQuiz.q: Which F-diagram route does handwashing with soap mainly block?
finalQuiz.explain: Handwashing removes germs from hands, blocking the fingers route from faeces to mouth.

finalQuiz.q: Why is a clean, covered toilet called the primary barrier?
options: It is the cheapest item in the home
It replaces the need for handwashing
It stops faeces reaching water, hands, flies and soil in the first place
It makes water safe to drink
finalQuiz.explain: Keeping faeces contained blocks every route at the source. Handwashing and safe water are still needed as secondary barriers.

finalQuiz.q: Which step comes last in the WHO handwashing method?
options: Use the towel to turn off the tap
finalQuiz.explain: After rinsing and drying, the towel is used to turn off the tap so clean hands do not touch a dirty tap.

finalQuiz.q: Weekly cleaning tasks take 180 minutes. Three people share them equally. How long does each person work?
Which dish washing method is most hygienic for a home without a sink?
options: Wash in soapy water, rinse in clean water, dry upside down on a raised rack
One basin for washing and rinsing everything
Wash in soapy water and stack on a floor mat
Wipe plates dry with the hand towel
finalQuiz.explain: A separate rinse removes soap and loosened dirt, and drying off the floor keeps plates clean.

finalQuiz.q: Water from a tanker looks clear. What should a family do before drinking it?
options: Treat it, for example by bringing it to a rolling boil, then store it covered
Store it in an open drum in the sun
finalQuiz.explain: Clear water can still contain germs. A rolling boil inactivates bacteria, viruses and protozoa, and covered storage keeps it safe.

finalQuiz.q: According to WHO, how is Lassa virus mainly passed to people?
options: Through contact with food or household items contaminated with rat urine or faeces
finalQuiz.explain: WHO says Lassa virus is primarily transmitted through food or household items contaminated with Mastomys rat urine or faeces.

finalQuiz.q: What should go into a covered bin instead of the toilet or pit latrine?
options: Wrapped sanitary pads and disposable nappies
finalQuiz.explain: Pads and nappies block pipes and fill pits. Wrap them and put them in a covered bin. Child faeces do go into the toilet.

finalQuiz.q: A family fills 20-litre buckets with waste: food 3 times, recyclables 2 times, other 2 times in a week. If they compost food and recycle, how much is left for collection?
finalQuiz.explain: Only the other waste remains: 2 x 20 = 40 litres, down from (3 + 2 + 2) x 20 = 140 litres.

finalQuiz.q: Which first aid is correct for a chemical splash in the eye?
options: Rub the eye to remove it
Add a few drops of milk
Rinse with plenty of clean running water and seek care
finalQuiz.explain: Rinse straight away with clean running water, holding the eyelids open, and keep rinsing on the way to care.

finalQuiz.q: A child with diarrhoea becomes very sleepy, has sunken eyes and has not passed urine for hours. What should the carer do?
options: Give an antibiotic from the market
Go to a health facility now; these are signs of dehydration
finalQuiz.explain: These are danger signs of dehydration. Go to care immediately and never give medicines without a health worker's advice.

finalQuiz.q: A cleaning job costs 10,000 naira in total. Adding 30% profit on cost, what is the price?
